units.content: Research State Restoration Protocol; preserve and reconstruct a research state so future work can resume from explicit assumptions, objects, dependencies, hypotheses, predictions, experiments and open questions rather than a prose summary.
Layered restoration artifact intended to reconstruct the research program from purpose through formal objects, hypotheses, predictions, experiments and later architecture layers.
Purpose/bootstrapping layer; supplies a restoration objective and organization, not empirical evidence or a scientific result.
States explicit starting axioms so later theory can be reconstructed and revised rather than treated as hidden assumptions.

Ten source-labelled axioms covering adaptive systems, feedback, representations, reachability, generators, resources/constraints, measurable consequences and the requirement that explanatory structure remain testable and revisable.
The source explicitly says axioms are not absolute truths; they are starting constraints for a minimal, testable, revisable framework.
AXIOM label != established truth; downstream reuse of an axiom does not create independent empirical support.
Defines the objects the framework talks about before specifying how they evolve.

content.adaptive_system: system changing internal state in response to feedback
content.generator: mechanism producing or improving search/transformation procedures

units.content: Ontology identifies objects/terms; it does not by itself establish dynamics, causal relations, measurements or empirical existence.
Definition layer only; semantic identity with same tokens in later layers is not automatic.
Specifies the framework's source-internal dependency/causal structure.

Source graph includes rho -> G_m -> A -> X -> P^reach -> C, with resources and constraints entering capability/reachability paths and generator changes propagating through adoption/execution before realized capability.
A generator-improvement chain is proposed in which deeper generator changes precede reachability/capability acceleration rather than capability being the primitive cause.
Resource scaling is represented as a distinct path to capability, allowing generator-driven and resource-driven growth to be separated conceptually.
This is a source-theory dependency graph; it is not a Program Consolidation map edge set and creates no cross-repository relation or authority.
Introduces mathematical variables and operators for the adaptive/reachability framework.
Defines source-local variables for state, generator quality, adoption, execution, reachable frontier, capability, resources, feedback and related transition quantities.
On this source surface Omega is represented as generator-improvement velocity, including the formulation Omega=dG_m/dt.
Provides mathematical transition/dependency relationships linking generator change, adoption/execution, reachable space and capability.
Formal vocabulary/model proposal; equations are not empirical observations or proved universal laws by compression.
Organizes the program's conjectures into an explicit hypothesis system.

Nine source-labelled hypotheses covering generator-first capability transitions, reachability expansion, adoption/execution mediation, representation effects, resource confounds, recursive improvement, causal mass and related adaptive-transition claims.
Each hypothesis is paired with observable/predictive consequences intended to discriminate it from alternative explanations.
Hypotheses include failure conditions and are intended to be broken by counterexamples, controls or missing predicted ordering.
The source explicitly states hypotheses are provisional and exist to generate experiments, not conclusions.
Creates a registry of predictions so theory can be tested prospectively rather than retrofitted after outcomes.
Registers source predictions about temporal ordering, generator change, reachability, resource controls, adoption/execution, representation and capability trajectories.
Predictions are to be compared with measurements, controls and counterfactual alternatives; failures should update the framework rather than be explained away.
The source explicitly states: predictions are not evidence.
Defines how candidate claims should be tested experimentally.
Protocol specifies controlled comparisons, baseline/resource controls, intervention variables, longitudinal measurement, ablation/counterfactual reasoning and falsification criteria.
Experiments are designed to test whether generator improvement precedes and contributes to reachability/capability acceleration beyond resource scaling.
Experimental design only; no execution record, measured result or support/falsification result is reported in this layer.
Defines a framework for evaluating historical/empirical cases under common variables and controls.

Cases should identify system, intervention, generator change, adoption/execution, reachability, capability, resource contribution and temporal ordering rather than treat innovation anecdotes as proof.
Source proposes historical/technological examples as candidate cases for analysis; examples illustrate the schema and do not constitute validated case results.
Empirical-case template/proposal; no completed historical dataset or validated cross-case result appears on this layer.
Formalizes how to distinguish generator effects from resources, baseline capability and other confounds.
Defines source-local counterfactual/intervention quantities, treatment/control contrasts and causal attribution targets for generator-driven capability change.
Uses counterfactual comparisons, do/intervention framing, matched controls, ablation, mediation and temporal ordering to identify whether generator change is causally relevant.
Observed capability growth alone is insufficient; the stronger target is generator-related causal contribution after controlling alternatives.
Causal-identification proposal; no identified causal estimate is reported.
Extends the framework with an alignment architecture for adaptive/self-improving systems.
Proposes monitoring, representation/goal tracking, feedback, correction and verification loops intended to preserve direction while capability changes.
Alignment is framed as a dynamic control problem rather than one-time obedience; capability growth and correction/control capacity must be tracked separately.
Architecture/theory proposal; does not establish that the proposed control loop is sufficient or implemented.
Attempts a source-internal unified architecture combining prior representation, generator, feedback, causal and alignment components.
Presents a combined layered/loop architecture intended to function as a compact bootloader for restoring the preceding research structure.
The source describes itself in unified/bootloader terms; this is source self-characterization, not supersession authority over Layers 1-11.
UNIFIED or COMPLETE language does not erase disagreements, branch-specific standing or provenance of earlier source layers.
Defines how a compressed/restored research state should be retrieved and reconstructed.
Proposes retrieval of purpose, axioms, ontology, formal objects, dependency structure, hypotheses, predictions, experiments and status in a reconstruction sequence.
Research memory should preserve generative structure and dependencies rather than only narrative summaries or final answers.
Retrieval/continuity protocol; no claim that successful restoration has been independently demonstrated.
Proposes an external anchor artifact capable of bootstrapping research-state recovery when conversational/internal context is unavailable.
Defines a self-contained external object containing enough identifiers, dependencies, core variables, hypotheses and retrieval directions to recover the research program.
Externalized memory is treated as a robustness mechanism against context loss; an anchor should reconstruct rather than invent missing state.
Proposed artifact design, not an independently tested restoration result.
Defines a protocol by which the framework could revise itself under empirical pressure.
Proposes generation of candidate framework modifications, explicit evaluation/falsification, comparison against prior state, retention of successful changes and preservation of provenance.
Framework mutations should be accepted because they improve prediction/explanation under tests, not because they are novel or more complex.
Self-improvement protocol proposal; no executed self-modification history is reported by this layer.
Translates prior conceptual research objects into a proposed implementation architecture.
Specifies candidate components/data structures for hypotheses, predictions, experiments, evidence, state restoration and update/validation flows.
Contains schema/example fields including a literal result value such as 'supported'; this is illustrative structured data, not an observed support result.
Frozen Markdown contains malformed or unclosed code-block style formatting; substantial semantic content remains recoverable.
Implementation architecture/specification only; the R09 frozen tree contains no corresponding runnable implementation artifact.
Proposes a multi-agent architecture for research generation, criticism, experimentation, synthesis and memory.
Separates candidate agents/roles for hypothesis generation, skeptical challenge, experiment design, evaluation, integration and archival/retrieval functions.
Multiple agents are intended to create internal challenge/diversity rather than convert agreement into truth automatically.
Frozen Markdown includes formatting irregularities while the intended architecture remains substantially readable.
Multi-agent research architecture proposal; no instantiated agent system or execution result is present.
Extends adaptive/intelligence concepts to civilization-scale systems.
Treats civilization as distributed information processing in which institutions, technologies, memory and coordination mechanisms can alter knowledge-generation and reachable futures.
Language, writing, science, institutions, computing and related structures are used as interpretive examples of civilization-level memory/generator effects.
Conceptual/civilizational architecture extension; historical examples are not source-reported validation results.
